name: traefik-manager
description: A web UI for managing Traefik routes, middlewares, services, and certificates. Supports multiple config files, API keys for mobile access, two-factor authentication, and config backups. Requires access to your Traefik dynamic config file and the Traefik API.

paths.name: Config Directory
paths.description: Stores manager.yml (settings, password, API keys) and the session signing key. Must be persistent.

paths.name: Backups Directory
paths.description: Timestamped backups of your dynamic config are saved here before every change.

paths.name: Certs Tab - acme.json
paths.description: Optional: path to your Traefik acme.json file on the host. Required for the Certs tab. Read-only is enough to see certificates and which of them nothing uses. Set it read-write, together with a Restart Method, to also remove certificates from the Certs tab.

paths.name: Static Config / Plugins Tab - traefik.yml
paths.description: Optional: path to your Traefik static config file (traefik.yml) on the host. Required for the Plugins tab and the Static Config editor. Mount read-write to allow editing; read-only enables the Plugins tab only. Also set the Static Config Path variable below to /app/traefik.yml.

paths.name: Logs Tab - access.log
paths.description: Optional: path to your Traefik access log file on the host. Required for the Logs tab. Enable access logging in traefik.yml first: accessLog: filePath: /logs/access.log. Mount read-only.

paths.name: Docker Socket (direct)
paths.description: Optional: mount the Docker socket for the direct socket restart method (RESTART_METHOD=socket). Host path: /var/run/docker.sock

paths.name: Restart Signals Volume
paths.description: Optional: only for Restart Method poison-pill. Map a shared path here and at the same target in your watcher container, then point Signal File Path inside it. Leave blank for the other restart methods.

ports.name: Web UI Port
ports.description: Port to access the Traefik Manager web UI.

variables.name: Traefik API URL
variables.description: URL of the Traefik API. Usually http://traefik:8080 when on the same Docker network.

variables.name: Traefik API Username
variables.description: Optional: basic-auth username for the Traefik API, if your API/dashboard is protected by a basicAuth middleware.

variables.name: Traefik API Password
variables.description: Optional: basic-auth password for the Traefik API. Only needed if TRAEFIK_API_USER is set.

variables.name: Domains
variables.description: Comma-separated list of base domains shown in the Add Route form. Example: example.com,home.lab

variables.name: Cert Resolver
variables.description: Default ACME certificate resolver name from your traefik.yml. Comma-separate multiple resolvers.

variables.name: Config File Path (single file)
variables.description: Path inside the container to your Traefik dynamic config file. Use this for a single config file. Mount the file via the path mapping below. Leave blank if using CONFIG_DIR or CONFIG_PATHS.

variables.name: Config Directory Path (multi-file)
variables.description: Path inside the container to a directory containing multiple .yml config files. All .yml files in this directory will be loaded. Use instead of CONFIG_PATH when managing multiple files. Leave blank if using CONFIG_PATH.

variables.name: Config Paths (explicit list)
variables.description: Comma-separated list of full config file paths inside the container. Use instead of CONFIG_PATH for 2-5 named files. Example: /app/config/routes.yml,/app/config/services.yml. Leave blank if using CONFIG_PATH or CONFIG_DIR.

variables.name: Static Config Path
variables.description: Path inside the container to the static config (traefik.yml) you mounted above. Set to /app/traefik.yml to enable the Static Config editor and Plugins tab. Leave blank if not mounting traefik.yml.

variables.name: Restart Method
variables.description: How Traefik Manager restarts Traefik after a static config change. Options: proxy (socket proxy - recommended), socket (direct Docker socket), poison-pill (signal file, requires watcher sidecar). Removing this field falls back to proxy, it does not turn restarts off.

variables.name: Traefik Container Name
variables.description: Name of the Traefik Docker container to restart. Used by the proxy and socket restart methods.

variables.name: Docker Host (socket proxy)
variables.description: Docker host URL for the socket proxy restart method. Example: tcp://socket-proxy:2375. Only set when RESTART_METHOD=proxy.

variables.name: Signal File Path (poison pill)
variables.description: Path to the signal file written by Traefik Manager to trigger a Traefik restart. Only used when RESTART_METHOD=poison-pill. Mount a shared volume to /signals in both this container and the watcher sidecar.

variables.name: Admin Password
variables.description: Optional: set a fixed admin password. If left empty a temporary password is generated on first start - check the container log for it.

variables.name: Cookie Secure
variables.description: Set to true when accessing Traefik Manager over HTTPS (e.g. behind a Traefik reverse proxy with TLS). Required for session cookies to work correctly over HTTPS.

variables.name: Auth Enabled
variables.description: Set to false to disable built-in login. Only use this when Traefik Manager is protected by an external auth provider such as Authentik or Authelia.

variables.name: CrowdSec LAPI URL
variables.description: Optional: CrowdSec Local API URL (e.g. http://crowdsec:8080) to enable the CrowdSec tab. Can also be set in Settings.

variables.name: CrowdSec API Key
variables.description: Optional: CrowdSec bouncer API key, used to read decisions. Generate with: cscli bouncers add traefik-manager

variables.name: CrowdSec Machine ID
variables.description: Optional: CrowdSec machine login, required to view Alerts and to unban (bouncer keys cannot). Create with: cscli machines add traefik-manager --auto

variables.name: CrowdSec Machine Password
variables.description: Optional: password for the CrowdSec machine login above. Found in /etc/crowdsec/local_api_credentials.yaml.

variables.name: Settings File Path
variables.description: Path inside the container to the Traefik Manager settings file. Change this if you want to store it separately from the dynamic config.

variables.name: Backup Directory Path
variables.description: Path inside the container where backups are written. Change this if you mount a custom backup volume at a different path.

variables.name: Inactivity Timeout (minutes)
variables.description: Minutes of inactivity before a non-remembered session is logged out.

variables.name: OTP Encryption Key
variables.description: Fernet key for encrypting the 2FA TOTP secret at rest. Auto-generated on first start if not set. Set this if you want to manage the key yourself or ensure it survives config volume replacement. Generate with: python3 -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"

variables.name: Secret Key
variables.description: Session signing key. Auto-generated on first start and saved to /app/config/.secret_key. Set this explicitly to ensure sessions survive a full config wipe, or to share a key across multiple instances.

variables.name: Trusted Proxy Hops
variables.description: How many reverse-proxy hops to trust when reading X-Forwarded-For. With Cloudflare in front of Traefik in front of this container, set 2 so the login and audit log record the real client. Set 0 to ignore the header entirely. Only count hops you actually control - each trusted hop is one more entry a client could forge.

variables.name: Skip Traefik API TLS Verification
variables.description: Set true when the Traefik API URL is https with a self-signed or Cloudflare Origin certificate.

variables.name: acme.json Path
variables.description: Path to acme.json inside the container, when it is not the default /app/acme.json. Accepts several files comma-separated, or a directory whose .json files are all read - Traefik writes one storage file per certificate resolver.

variables.name: Access Log Path
variables.description: Path to the Traefik access log inside the container, when it is not the default /app/logs/access.log.

variables.name: Plugins Directory
variables.description: Path to Traefik's local plugins directory, for the Plugins tab.

variables.name: Backup Retention
variables.description: Keep only the last N backups per config file. 0 keeps every backup.

variables.name: GeoIP Database Path
variables.description: Path to a custom MaxMind-format .mmdb for IP geolocation. Leave empty to use the free DB-IP Lite database, downloaded on demand. Lookups run locally - no IP leaves the server.

variables.name: Log Level
variables.description: Logging verbosity. One of debug, info, warning, error.

variables.name: Base Path
variables.description: Serve Traefik Manager under a sub path instead of its own hostname, for example /tm. Leave blank to serve at the root.

variables.name: CrowdSec Alert Limit
variables.description: How many CrowdSec alerts to read at once. Leave blank for the default of 500.

variables.name: CrowdSec Client Certificate
variables.description: Path inside the container to a TLS client certificate for the CrowdSec LAPI, when it requires mTLS instead of an API key.

variables.name: CrowdSec Client Key
variables.description: Path inside the container to the private key for the CrowdSec client certificate.

variables.name: CrowdSec CA Certificate
variables.description: Path inside the container to the CA that signed the CrowdSec LAPI certificate.

variables.name: CrowdSec Connect Timeout
variables.description: Seconds to wait for the CrowdSec LAPI to accept a connection. Leave blank for the default.

variables.name: CrowdSec Read Timeout
variables.description: Seconds to wait for a CrowdSec LAPI response. Leave blank for the default.

variables.name: OIDC Enabled
variables.description: Set true to sign in with an OpenID Connect provider such as Authentik, Authelia or Keycloak.

variables.name: OIDC Provider URL
variables.description: Issuer URL of your OIDC provider, for example https://auth.example.com/application/o/traefik-manager/

variables.name: OIDC Client ID
variables.description: Client ID issued by your OIDC provider.

variables.name: OIDC Client Secret
variables.description: Client secret issued by your OIDC provider.

variables.name: OIDC Display Name
variables.description: Name shown on the sign in button, for example Authentik.

variables.name: OIDC Allowed Emails
variables.description: Comma-separated list of email addresses allowed to sign in.

variables.name: OIDC Allowed Groups
variables.description: Comma-separated list of groups allowed to sign in.

variables.name: OIDC Groups Claim
variables.description: Name of the token claim that carries group membership. Defaults to groups.

variables.name: OIDC Allow Any Authenticated
variables.description: Set true to let anyone your provider authenticates sign in, instead of listing emails or groups.

variables.name: OIDC Auto Sign In
variables.description: Set true to send visitors straight to the provider instead of showing the login form.

variables.name: Agent API Rate Limit
variables.description: Requests per minute allowed on the agent API. Leave blank for the default.

variables.name: Extra CA Bundle
variables.description: Path inside the container to a CA bundle, when Traefik or CrowdSec use a private certificate authority.
